newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Don't assume EMU will start on time - Buba's Gaddum.
newsitem.headline: Don't assume EMU will start on time - Buba's Gaddum.

text.p: Bundesbank Vice President Johann Wilhelm Gaddum warned against assuming Economic and Monetary Union will start on schedule in 1999.
"It would be dangerous to act as if the decision had already been made," Gaddum told Reuters at the World Economic Forum in Davos. "There will not be EMU at any price."
The most important thing is ensuring the single euro currency is credible, he said, adding it would not automatically inherit the credibility of the mark or other currencies.
Its credibility depends on an independent European central bank, strict adherence to convergence criteria and a convincing selection of participating countries in early 1998, he said.
He said there was no inflationary danger in Germany at the moment, although the dollar's recent rise would tend to make import prices rise.
"But domestic demand is growing so weakly that the leeway for passing on these price increases is very small," he said.
